A compact reference for radio controls, ranges, settings, and common effects.
For full instructions, see [textlink="AN/PRC-117G Radio" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] and [textlink="Field Headsets" link="AU14CommsHeadsets"].

### AN/PRC operator training
The AN/PRC control panel can be used by:
- [bold]GOVFOR and OPFOR[/bold] - Commander, Adjutant, staff officers, engineering officers, intelligence officers, synthetics, squad leaders, Fireteam Leaders, and Radio Traffic Operators. - [bold]CLF[/bold] - Cell Leader and Radio Operator. - Anyone who has read a [bold]field radio operator's pamphlet[/bold].
The handset can be used by anyone, trained or not.

### What anchors a combat net?
Faction combat nets, including squad, command, intelligence, JTAC, and MP, require relay coverage from at least one of the following:
- a powered AN/PRC worn by a trained operator - a deployed retransmission station - a command-post antenna mast - a powered communications array - a vehicle radio aboard a dropship or other vehicle - a field antenna mast - a staked CLF clandestine base station or relay set, for CLF nets - a mast or array carrying a CLF feeder tap, for CLF nets
Colony and civilian channels are not relay-gated.
## Net splicing
A CLF Radio Operator with a [bold]net splice kit[/bold] can add the cell's nets to a mast or communications array.
Splicing does not disable the host. Its original nets continue working normally.

### Splice rules
- A probe reads zero when the nearest carrier is more than 30 positions away. - A lock succeeds when it is within 4 positions of the carrier. - Each probe adds 1.5% detection. - A missed lock adds 30% detection and consumes 2 probes. - Running out of probes or filling the detection meter fails the attempt. - A failed junction remains faulted for 90 seconds and cannot be spliced again during that time. - The mast sparks while the splice is being worked and while faulted. - Anyone can remove an installed tap in eight seconds and recover a CLF fill card from it.

[bold]Function[/bold]
[bold]Benefits[/bold]

Frequency hopping
Reduces jamming by one tier and permits transmission inside jammer fields.

0.75x battery use and no DF signature while secured.

0.5x battery use.
Readable by compatible receivers, increases jamming by one tier, and has the largest DF signature.

PT is always transmitted in the clear.

## Squelch
Squelch controls how much damaged or noisy traffic the radio allows through.
It does [bold]not[/bold] improve the signal itself. Raising it simply hides progressively weaker or more degraded transmissions.
[bold]SQL[/bold]
[bold]Filtering[/bold]
[bold]0[/bold]
Passes all traffic, including heavy static.
[bold]1[/bold]
Suppresses heavy static and undecodable encrypted traffic.
[bold]2[/bold]
Suppresses medium jammer degradation.
[bold]3[/bold]
Default. Suppresses light jammer degradation and heavily broken fringe-range traffic.
[bold]4[/bold]
Maximum filtering. Even lightly degraded long-range traffic is suppressed.
Lower squelch lets more degraded traffic through.
Higher squelch gives you a quieter receiver, but weak stations may disappear entirely.
## COMSEC controls
[bold]Action[/bold]
[bold]Result[/bold]
Insert fill card
Secures compatible faction traffic in FH, SC, and CT.
[bold]ZEROIZE[/bold]
Ejects the loaded fill card without destroying it.
[bold]DESTROY[/bold]
Permanently destroys the loaded card.
[bold]RECRYPTO[/bold]
Supersedes all older cards from that faction, including captured cards. Requires command authority: Commander, Adjutant, or Advisor.
Captured current card
Allows compatible secured traffic from that faction to be decoded until they perform a recrypto.
Replacement fill cards are available through the normal supply system.
## Direction finding
The following transmissions create a direction-finding signature, from highest to lowest risk:
1. PT traffic 2. faction-net traffic sent without a matching fill 3. secured FH traffic
Secured SC and CT traffic produce no DF signature.
Repeated signature-producing transmissions from the same location increase the chance of detection.
DF risk begins falling again after roughly one minute without another qualifying transmission.
[bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] reports which stations receive your active net clearly or degraded.
When used inside a jammer field, it also reports a bearing toward the strongest jammer.

## Net log
Stores the last [bold]50[/bold] radio entries.
Traffic from other factions is marked [bold]INTERCEPT[/bold].
[bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] prints the complete log.
[bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] prints only intercepted traffic.
